question: Скільки днів оплачуваної відпустки на рік я маю?
answer: Це залежить від стажу та типу зайнятості. Повна зайнятість: 0–3 роки — 80 годин, 3–5 років — 120 годин, понад 5 років — 160 годин на рік. Неповна зайнятість: 40 годин на рік. Відпускні години нараховуються на річницю дати прийому і мають використовуватися протягом року. Невикористана відпустка не переноситься на наступний рік і не виплачується при звільненні. Відпусткою можна користуватися після 60 днів роботи, мінімальний блок — 4 години.
expected_answer: Відпустка рахується в годинах: 80 годин (0–3 роки стажу), 120 (3–5 років), 160 (5+ років); part-time — 40 годин.

question: Скільки днів оплачуваної відпустки на рік я маю?
answer: Скільки часу ви вже працюєте в компанії (ваш стаж)?
expected_answer: 24 календарні дні після 6 місяців безперервної роботи; до того — пропорційно відпрацьованому часу.

question: Скільки днів оплачуваної відпустки на рік я маю?
answer: Працівники Costa Rica мають 18 календарних днів оплачуваної щорічної відпустки після щонайменше 50 тижнів безперервної роботи. До цього відпустка нараховується пропорційно тривалості роботи. Окремі категорії (наприклад, вагітні та жінки після пологів, співробітники з інвалідністю, студенти, які готуються до іспитів, а також ті, хто нещодавно відслужив в армії) можуть отримати повну відпустку раніше. Відпустку потрібно погодити за два тижні, а залишок невикористаної відпустки на кінець року виплачується грошима.
expected_answer: 18 календарних днів після 50 тижнів безперервної роботи; до того — пропорційно відпрацьованому часу.

question: How long do I have to work before I am entitled to paid vacation?
answer: You become eligible to use paid vacation time after 60 days of employment. Full-time employees get 80 hours for 0-3 years of service, 120 hours for 3-5 years, and 160 hours for 5+ years. Part-time employees get 40 hours. Vacation hours are front-loaded on your anniversary date.
expected_answer: New employees can use vacation after 60 days of employment.

question: How long do I have to work before I am entitled to paid vacation?
answer: You are entitled to 24 calendar days of paid annual leave after completing at least 6 months of continuous employment. During your first 6 months, you accrue vacation pro-rated for the length of your employment. Some categories of employees, such as certain parents, employees with disabilities, and those hired after military service, can take full-length leave before completing the 6 months.
expected_answer: The full 24 days after 6 months of continuous employment; before that a pro-rated vacation (some categories get the full leave earlier).

question: How long do I have to work before I am entitled to paid vacation?
answer: You are entitled to 18 calendar days of paid annual leave after completing at least 50 weeks of continuous employment. During your first 50 weeks, you accrue vacation pro-rated for the length of your employment. Certain categories get full-duration leave before completing the 50 weeks, including female employees before and after pregnancy and childbirth (or with two or more children under 15, or a child with disabilities), employees with disabilities, employees whose wives are on maternity leave, employees hired after military service, and employees studying who want leave for exams or a thesis. These rules apply to Costa Rica employees.
expected_answer: The full 18 days after 50 weeks of continuous employment; before that a pro-rated vacation (some categories get the full leave earlier).

question: What is the minimum amount of vacation I can take at once?
answer: The minimum amount of vacation you can take at once is 4 hours. Vacations may be used in minimum 4-hour increments.
expected_answer: Vacation may be used in minimum 4-hour increments.

question: What is the minimum amount of vacation I can take at once?
answer: For Ukraine office employees, the main continuous part of annual leave must be at least 14 calendar days. Any remaining part of the leave can be requested in minimum 3-day increments, or in minimum 1-day increments during martial law. Two weeks' notice is required before taking vacation leave, and the employer may decline to split the leave as you wish.
expected_answer: The main part must be at least 14 calendar days, the rest in minimum 3-day increments; during martial law vacation can be taken in 1-day increments.

question: What is the minimum amount of vacation I can take at once?
answer: In Costa Rica, the minimum block you can take at once depends on how the leave is split. Your main continuous part of annual leave must be at least 14 calendar days. Any remaining part of your vacation can be requested in increments of at least 3 days. Vacation requests also require two weeks' notice. The employer may decide not to split the leave as you wish.
expected_answer: The main part must be at least 14 calendar days, the rest in minimum 3-day increments (no martial-law exception).

question: Which public holidays does the company observe?
answer: It Company observes six holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day. Full-time employees receive one day's pay at their regular straight-time rate, and part-time employees receive 4 hours' pay. To receive holiday pay, you must be present at work on your last scheduled day before the holiday and the first scheduled day after it, and employees on unpaid leave do not receive holiday pay.
expected_answer: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, Christmas Day.

question: Which public holidays does the company observe?
answer: The handbook lists six US holidays that the company observes: New Year Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving Day, and Christmas Day. Employees also get 5 floating holidays that they can use to celebrate Ukrainian public holidays at their discretion. If a holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it is observed the following Monday. Four days' notice is required before taking a paid holiday, and no more than one paid holiday can be taken in any 30-day period.
expected_answer: Six US holidays (New Year, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas) plus 5 floating days for Ukrainian public holidays.

question: Which public holidays does the company observe?
answer: It Company observes these six Costa Rican public holidays: New Year's Day (January 1), Juan Santamaría Day (April 11), Labour Day (May 1), Guanacaste Day (July 25), Independence Day (September 15), and Christmas Day (December 25). If a holiday falls on a Saturday or Sunday, it is observed the following Monday. Employees also get 7 additional floating holidays they can use for any other public or personal holiday.
expected_answer: New Year's Day, Juan Santamaría Day, Labour Day, Guanacaste Day, Independence Day (September 15), Christmas Day.

question: How many floating holidays do I get?
answer: You get 5 (five) additional floating holidays, which you can request to celebrate any Ukrainian public holiday at your discretion. No more than 1 paid holiday day off can be taken in a 30-day period, and four days' notice is required before taking one.
expected_answer: 5 floating holidays for Ukrainian public holidays; no more than 1 per 30 days, 4 days' notice.

question: How many floating holidays do I get?
answer: You get 7 (seven) floating holidays. You can use them to celebrate any public or personal holiday of your choice. Four days' notice is required before taking a paid holiday or day off, and no more than 1 paid holiday day off can be taken in any 30-day period. These rules apply to employees in Costa Rica.
expected_answer: 7 floating holidays; no more than 1 per 30 days, 4 days' notice.

question: How is sick leave paid?
answer: This applies to employees who work in New York City. Safe and sick time is paid at the same rate the employee earns when using it, unless applicable law requires otherwise, but never less than the applicable minimum wage. Payment is made no later than the payday for the next regular payroll period after the time was used. Paid safe and sick time doesn't count as hours worked for overtime calculations. Employees get 40 hours at the start of employment and 40 hours at the start of each calendar year, and they can't use more than 40 hours in a calendar year. I don't have information on how sick days are paid for employees outside New York City.
expected_answer: Employees working in New York City get 40 hours of paid safe and sick time per calendar year, paid at their regular rate; longer off-the-job illness — statutory short-term disability, 50% of average wages up to $170 a week from the 8th day.

question: How is sick leave paid?
answer: Sick leave in Ukraine is paid as follows. You are entitled to up to four months of paid sick leave for illness or injury, provided it is confirmed by a sick leave certificate from a medical institution. The employer pays the first five days, and the Social Insurance Fund pays the rest. The Fund's rate depends on your seniority: under 6 months, minimum wage; 0-3 years, 50% of average salary; 3-5 years, 60%; 5-8 years, 70%; 8+ years, 100%.
expected_answer: Up to 4 months with a medical certificate; the first 5 days are paid by the employer, the rest by the Social Insurance Fund at 50–100% of average salary depending on seniority.

question: How is sick leave paid?
answer: Sick leave is paid for up to four months if the illness or injury is confirmed by a sick leave certificate from the CCSS or another medical institution. For the first three days, the employer pays 50% of the employee's salary. From the fourth day, the CCSS pays 60% of the employee's average salary. This applies to employees in Costa Rica.
expected_answer: For the first 3 days the employer pays 50% of salary; from the 4th day the CCSS pays 60% of average salary.

question: How many days of paternity leave do fathers get, and is it paid?
answer: The handbook has no separate paternity leave policy, so it doesn't specify a number of days for fathers. The closest provision is State Paid Family Leave (PFL), which covers bonding with a child during the first 12 months after birth, adoption, or foster placement, for any eligible employee regardless of gender. It allows up to 12 weeks within a 52-week period. It is partially paid: 67% of your average weekly wage, up to 67% of the state average weekly wage, and it is funded entirely through employee payroll contributions. Eligibility requires a regular schedule of 20+ hours per week and 26 consecutive weeks of employment (or under 20 hours per week and 175 days worked). The company may also let you supplement PFL with paid time off. Please contact HR to confirm whether any additional paternity leave applies to you.
expected_answer: No separate paternity leave; Paid Family Leave gives up to 12 weeks to bond with a child, paid at 67% of the average weekly wage.

question: How many days of paternity leave do fathers get, and is it paid?
answer: Fathers are entitled to two weeks (14 days) of unpaid leave for the birth of a child. Fathers can also take leave from the mother's maternity leave if she has already returned to work, which requires a request to the Head of Representative Office with supporting documents.
expected_answer: 2 weeks of unpaid leave; a father can also take over the mother's maternity leave if she has returned to work.

question: How many days of paternity leave do fathers get, and is it paid?
answer: Fathers in Costa Rica get eight (8) days of paid leave for the birth of a child. Fathers may also take leave from the mother's maternity leave if she has already returned to work, which requires a request to the Head of Representative Office and supporting documents.
expected_answer: 8 days of paid leave; a father can also take over the mother's maternity leave if she has returned to work.

question: Do I get a 13th-month salary?
answer: Yes. Employees in Costa Rica receive an annual 13th-month salary (aguinaldo) equal to one twelfth of the total salary earned from December 1 of the previous year to November 30 of the current year. It is paid no later than December 20.
expected_answer: Yes — the aguinaldo, one twelfth of the salary earned from December 1 to November 30, paid no later than December 20.
